advisory.title: Preventing Card Testing: Spot It Early, Stop It Fast
advisory.rights_note: Short attributed excerpts quoted for analysis; full text remains at the source URL.
advisory.excerpt:
Card testing is when fraudsters attempt to validate stolen card details by making $0 or low-dollar transactions.
Fraud tactics are evolving, and card testing attacks are increasingly targeting e-commerce and mobile checkout.
They run $0 or small-dollar attempts at real merchants to confirm a card is active and may retry to fill in missing details (like CVV or expiration date).
Automated testing is the most common.
Many different card numbers attempted in a short time—often from the same IP address, device or small set of sessions.
More failed payments than usual, including repeated CVV or expiration date mismatch errors.
Multiple attempts on the same card or session where only one field changes each time (for example, cycling CVV or expiration date values).
A wave of $0 authorizations or low-dollar transactions used to test cards with minimal cost and attention.

dataset.description: Synthetic payments scenario (~3.4% fraud) with velocity, decline, card-present, time-of-day, device, SIM-change, credential-reset, and new-payee features. Three fraud modes: high-value misuse, injected card testing, and injected SIM-swap account takeover.
dataset.limitations: Fully synthetic. The card-testing and SIM-swap account-takeover patterns were injected to demonstrate how the workflow surfaces coverage gaps, and legitimate look-alikes were added for each; results do not measure real-world detection.

findings.summary: The advisory discusses card testing attacks where fraudsters execute automated $0 or low-dollar transactions and wave-like authorization tests accompanied by failed payments (such as CVV or expiration mismatches) across shared IP addresses and devices to verify stolen card details.
behaviors: Fraudsters attempt to validate stolen card details by making $0 or low-dollar transactions.
Many different card numbers attempted in a short time from the same IP address, device, or session.
More failed payments than usual, including repeated CVV or expiration date mismatch errors.
Multiple attempts on the same card or session where only one field changes each time.
indicators: High frequency of transactions in a short time window
Low dollar amounts ($0 to small amounts)
High volume of failed payments or declined attempts
Same IP address or device making multiple card attempts
testable_hypotheses: Transactions with low amounts and high declined attempt counts in 24 hours indicate card testing activity.
High transaction velocity combined with low transaction amounts identifies automated card testing.
uncertainties: IP address and device identifier fields are absent from the evaluation schema, preventing direct testing of shared-infrastructure indicators.
Synthetic data distributions may not fully replicate live e-commerce card-testing velocity patterns.

agent_conclusion.rationale: The advisory describes card testing behaviors involving automated low-dollar transactions and failed authorization attempts. While the exact IP/device indicators cannot be tested directly due to missing fields, transaction velocity and amount fields cover the core mechanics. An existing approved rule (AGT-a48565d1-1) already addresses rapid low-dollar transactions (transactions_1h >= 5 and amount < 5). Evaluating a complementary candidate rule targeting declined attempts and low amounts (AGT-ebe2cf96-1) showed very modest recall gains with largely overlapping coverage. Therefore, the intelligence is substantially covered by existing rules.
limitations: Dataset lacks IP address and device fingerprinting fields mentioned in the advisory.
Candidate rule adds minimal incremental recall over the existing approved rule set.

rule.name: Declined Low Dollar Card Testing
rule.rationale: Captures card testing attacks exhibiting multiple declined attempts combined with low-dollar transaction amounts, reflecting the advisory's observation of failed payments and small-dollar transaction waves.

baseline_rule.name: High transaction amount baseline
baseline_rule.description: Flags a transaction when its amount is at least 1,500 synthetic currency units.
baseline_rule.rationale: A simple, documented starting point for comparing candidate rules. The threshold is illustrative and is not calibrated for real financial data.

reference_rules.name: High transaction amount baseline
reference_rules.description: Flags a transaction when its amount is at least 1,500 synthetic currency units.
reference_rules.rationale: A simple, documented starting point for comparing candidate rules. The threshold is illustrative and is not calibrated for real financial data.

reference_rules.name: Rapid Low Dollar Transactions Card Testing
reference_rules.rationale: Detects card testing attacks characterized by multiple transactions in a short time window (transactions_1h >= 5) with small-dollar amounts (amount < 5).
